Fire Dept. seeks community input on disaster preparedness

Piedmont Post · October 7, 2026 · 2 min read

The Piedmont Fire Department is asking community members to complete a brief disaster preparedness survey by October 30. The survey will measure changes since 2024 and help guide future preparedness efforts.

Preparedness knowledge and actions have changed since the city’s first community survey in 2024. This survey will help the city understand how prepared the community is for earthquakes, wildfires, and other disasters.

The survey should take about 5-7 minutes to complete and is available at piedmont.ca.gov/DisasterSurvey. The city’s 2024 survey showed that many respondents recognized disaster risk but had not taken some basic preparedness steps.

Among respondents:

  • 73% were registered for AC Alert
  • 22% had a current household emergency communication plan
  • 34% had a current two-week emergency water supply
  • 27% felt confident or very confident in their knowledge of how to prepare for disasters

This year’s survey revisits many of these measures and includes new questions about how the city’s preparedness efforts have developed. This includes earthquake safety and steps that residents can take to minimize wildfire risks at home.

The survey will ask where people turn for information during an emergency, what gets in the way of becoming better prepared, and what kinds of resources would be most useful.

Since the 2024 survey, Piedmont Fire has expanded preparedness outreach and community engagement, including:

  • Updating Piedmont’s Local Hazard Mitigation Plan with extensive community participation
  • Increasing education about wildfire home hardening and defensible space, including a series of presentations to community groups
  • Conducting a practical wildfire evacuation exercise in the Blair/Scenic/Alta neighborhood and creating an at-home evacuation exercise available to all households
  • Continuing year-round outreach on emergency alerts, evacuation readiness, and household preparedness

The survey data will help the city evaluate where the work is having an impact and what gaps remain. It will also establish a stronger baseline for earthquake preparedness as Piedmont Fire looks to expand outreach in this area.

Results will help guide future communications, educational resources, exercises, and community programs. Complete the survey by October 30 at piedmont.ca.gov/DisasterSurvey. For resources and information about preparing for disasters, visit piedmont.ca.gov/Disaster.
